Nothing to do with your PR but I just realised, the fact that composition layers are positioned with quaternion and position means we're loosing scale.

There was a bug report of that some time ago around world_scale not being applied, and this explains why :)

cc @dsnopek

I'm not sure it makes sense to apply scale to composition layers. Or, at least, it's not what I would want in like 99% of circumstances, so I don't think it should happen automatically. Like, in the Alice demo you wouldn't want your settings panel to change size depending on whether your character is big or small - it should be sized based on real world sizes in either case.

To really scale a composition layer you'd need to scale the size of the shape (quad, equirect, cylinder). I suppose we could have a checkbox that, if enabled, would lead to multiplying the shape sizes by the world scale? But I really don't think this will be very commonly used

I'm all for style consistency! Updated :smile: 

I opted to remove `break;` after default cases in all `switch` blocks in the files I touched in the spirit of keeping the style consistent.

Do we still need the call to `update_transform()` given that `_update_pose_space()` also calls `composition_layer_extension->composition_layer_set_transform(...)`.

Following on that thought, do we need to deprecate and remove `update_transform()` and just use `_update_pose_space()` instead?

Good point! How do we feel about replacing the logic in `update_transform()` with what I've added in `_update_pose_space()` and deleting `_update_pose_space()`? 
I worry that because `update_transform()` will now do more than just updating the transform, the name might be misleading?

Indeed, this for me has always been the issue around scaling in VR, and I think lies at the source of us always running into trouble when trying to scale the XROrigin3D node.

In this case I just don't think we can say anything sensible about the use cases until we actually have this in the wild and people actually run into issue. If so we can always either add something to store scale, or simply recommend people to add a bit of extra code to resize the composition layers dimensions accordingly.

I think we'll find out that both use cases are valid, those where we don't want to scale, and those where we do. It's easier to add some additional scale logic if you need it, than remove scale logic when you don't :)

Seeing that we're now setting our transform based on our pose space, I think the update transform logic may even be broken without doing this change.

My gut feeling is that it is the correct behaviour to do exactly as you say, just move the logic from `_update_pose_space` into `update_transform` and be consistent in how we set the transform.
This suggestion makes sense to me! But I agree with Bastiaan that the code should move into `update_transform()` because it's the better function name
Removed `_update_pose_space()` and moved the logic contained in that function to `update_transform()`. Also replaced all calls of `_update_pose_space()` with `update_transform()`.

We don't actually support putting composition layers in global space yet - that's what @m4gr3d's PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114324 does.

For both pose spaces, we are still using `get_transform()`, it's just what the transform is relative to is different (either the camera or the `XROrigin3D`)

So, this probably shouldn't actually use my code suggestion above, we can just call `get_transform()` outside of the `switch` statement
